# Proposal: Fractional AI Governance Advisor

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Fractional AI Governance Advisor, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Client Profile Block v1.0 and discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, with about 1,100 staff. The Client has not completed a prior Academy program, so this proposal starts from the Profile Block alone.

The Client's AI use is at the piloting stage. A customer service chatbot is deployed on the support portal. AI visual inspection is being piloted on the German production line. AI sales forecasting is planned for next year. The stated regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. In June 2026, an internal audit finding recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems.

Your stated objective is clear: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." ISO/IEC 42001 work is expected to start next year, but no start date has been fixed. The Client lists ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 as incumbent frameworks. This proposal does not assume what registers, controls or records exist under them. Whether existing management system material can support AI governance is Unknown and will be assessed at intake.

Three constraints shape the plan:
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.
- The approved budget is up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

## 2. The Case for Continuous Fractional Advisory at the Piloting Stage

At the piloting stage, governance decisions are made alongside technical ones. A one-off assessment would describe the Client's position at a single moment. It would not stay with the Client while the visual inspection pilot moves toward production, while sales forecasting is scoped and while ISO/IEC 42001 work begins.

A fractional advisor provides continuity across these transitions. Governance artifacts mature in step with the systems they govern, and the executive team has a consistent point of reference when decisions arise between scheduled reviews.

The engagement is grounded in three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, and Final Liability rests with the Human. In practice, this means pacing deployment to the readiness of governance, making each decision with documented intent, and keeping accountability with named people at Tamarack Instruments rather than with the advisor or the system.

The working frameworks are:
- **GRC Workbook** (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) for governance, risk and compliance structure.
- **Slow AI Kitchen** (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) for deliberate implementation practice.
- **AI Governance for Boards** (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) for executive and board-layer material where required.

## 3. Annual Arc

The engagement start date is Unknown. Quarters one and two are sequenced so that governance tied to visual inspection is in place ahead of the Q2 2027 production target. A later start would compress that window, and we would discuss this at intake.

No external certification audit date exists. That date is Unknown and flagged for intake. Audit preparation therefore builds gradually rather than peaking against a fixed deadline.

**Quarter 1: Stabilize.**
- Respond to the June 2026 internal audit finding by establishing an AI system inventory that covers the deployed chatbot, the visual inspection pilot and the planned sales forecasting use case.
- Agree on governance roles, decision rights and a risk assessment approach using the GRC Workbook.
- Prepare questions on EU AI Act classification of each use case for external counsel to verify.

**Quarter 2: Govern the Production Decision.**
- Complete pre-production governance for visual inspection, including risk assessment, human oversight arrangements and documented go or no-go criteria.
- Prepare material so the Client can hold works council consultation in good time where a system touches production staff. Whether and when the visual inspection deployment triggers consultation is a matter for the Client and its counsel.

**Quarter 3: Deepen.**
- Apply the governance model to planned sales forecasting before it is built.
- Review the chatbot against the EU data residency constraint. Whether the chatbot processes customer data and where it is hosted is currently Unknown.
- Begin an ISO/IEC 42001 readiness gap assessment once the start date is fixed.

**Quarter 4: Assure and Evolve.**
- Mature evidence collection toward ISO/IEC 42001 readiness.
- Support internal audit readiness against the AI governance artifacts produced during the year.
- Prepare the year-two options.

## 4. Cadence and Access Model

The engagement includes four recurring elements:
- **Monthly executive advisory session:** decisions, risks and direction.
- **Monthly working session with the governance team:** artifact development and implementation guidance.
- **Asynchronous availability:** for defined question categories, with response windows agreed at intake.
- **Quarterly governance review:** progress against the annual arc and readiness status.

The Profile Block lists the General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors as audience roles. Who attends each session and who forms the governance team is Unknown and will be confirmed at intake.

## 5. Scope and Out of Scope

**In scope:**
- Governance evolution
- Implementation guidance
- Audit preparation
- AI strategy
- Executive decision support

**Out of scope:**
- Legal advice
- Certification body functions
- Staff augmentation
- Incident command

The advisor is not counsel of record. Legal questions, including EU AI Act and GDPR interpretation, route to the Client's external counsel. Regulatory developments raised during the engagement are flagged for counsel verification and are not offered as settled advice.

ISO/IEC 42001 work is described in readiness terms only. This proposal makes no promise of a certification or audit outcome.

## 6. Investment

The program fee is US$10,000 per month for twelve months, renewable.

The stated approved budget is up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. The Client's fiscal year dates are Unknown. As a result, it is Unknown how many monthly fees would fall within this fiscal year and how many in the next. We ask that this be confirmed so the commitment can be matched to the approved budget before signature. The program duration and price are fixed.
